tasks.instruction: The volley should fire at most the number of shots given as the second parameter (each shot costs 3 ammo and needs at least 3), and return the ammo left.
tasks.note: Loop count was a fixed 3; it must be the shot limit parameter. Wrong edit uses the ammo as the count.

tasks.instruction: Count the leading space characters (32) of the six-character line; a line of only spaces has indent 6.
tasks.note: Loop cap must equal the line length 6; 7 wraps the index and counts the first space again.

tasks.instruction: Return how many ticks a three-phase traffic light starting at the first parameter's phase needs to reach the goal phase given by the second parameter (at most 3).
tasks.note: The stop predicate's extra must be the goal phase, not the start phase. Wrong edit swaps start and goal both.

tasks.instruction: The heater must keep running only while the temperature is strictly below the setpoint (third parameter); reaching the setpoint stops it.
tasks.note: Stop predicate of the ramp loop: le overshoots; wrong edit swaps the operands.

tasks.instruction: The step should peel off base-8 digits instead of decimal digits: add the lowest octal digit to the running sum and drop it from the number.
tasks.note: Both the remainder and the quotient must use 8. Wrong edit changes only the remainder.

tasks.instruction: Account for a 3-minute warm-up: the time already used must start at 3 before any job runs, so fewer jobs may fit in the budget.
tasks.note: Start state of the loop record is (jobs done, minutes used); the warm-up goes in field 1. Wrong edit puts it in field 0.

tasks.instruction: Each tournament round pairs players and an odd player gets a bye, so the players left after a round is the count halved rounding up.
tasks.note: Loop step must round up: (n+1)/2. Wrong edit adds 2.

tasks.instruction: The scan must accept every decimal digit character '0' to '9' (48 to 57) at the current position and nothing else.
tasks.note: Stop predicate of a digit-prefix parser excluded '9'. Wrong edit also accepts ':'.

tasks.instruction: Dozenal digits ten and eleven must be written as the letters 'A' and 'B' respectively.
tasks.note: Text lookup table change; index wraps modulo 12.

tasks.instruction: Each size letter should cover 300 ml: 0-299 ml is S, 300-599 M, 600-899 L, 900-1199 X.
tasks.note: Index arithmetic into a size-letter string.

tasks.instruction: The packet header is now 'HDR2' instead of 'HDR'; the checksum must add every header byte to the payload value.
tasks.note: H=72, D=68, R=82, '2'=50. Wrong edit changes the text but still sums three bytes.

tasks.instruction: Decode instead of encode: the letter should be the one three places earlier in the 12-letter alphabet, wrapping around from 'A' to the end.
tasks.note: Going back 3 modulo 12 is adding 9; subtracting 3 wraps modulo 2^32 (not a multiple of 12) for small indexes.

tasks.instruction: Return the first letter printed on a phone key: key 2 is 'A', key 3 is 'D', up to key 9 which is 'W'.
tasks.note: Index offset into a text table.

tasks.instruction: The check should also accept the division sign '/', so all four characters of the operator string count as operators.
tasks.note: Index 4 wraps to 0 ('+'), so the wrong edit never matches '/'.

tasks.instruction: Read one price in cents and write the price including 8% tax (price plus price times 8 divided by 100, rounded down), not just the tax.
tasks.note: Multiplying by 108 overflows for large prices where the reference does not.

tasks.instruction: Read the old and new meter readings; write the old reading first and then the usage (new minus old).
tasks.note: Two writes threaded through the token in order. Wrong edit writes them reversed.

tasks.instruction: Write the scoreboard as one array with puts: the home score (second parameter) first, then the away score (third parameter).
tasks.note: puts writes the length 2 first. Wrong edit writes the scores without the length.

tasks.instruction: Write the status code (second parameter) before the 'OK' message, not after it.
tasks.note: Reorder token operations. Wrong edit keeps the old trailing write.

tasks.instruction: Read two words and pass each one through the emit helper, the first word read first.
tasks.note: Token passed through an earlier helper twice. Wrong edit emits the words in reverse.

tasks.instruction: Read a length in inches and write it as feet first, then the leftover inches.
tasks.note: Argument order into a token-taking helper. Wrong edit swaps the computations but keeps the call, so the output stays reversed.

tasks.instruction: Read two door sensor words (zero means closed, anything else open) and write 1 when both doors are in the same state, 0 otherwise.
tasks.note: Compares two bools with eq. Wrong edit compares the raw words.

tasks.instruction: Add the amount (fourth parameter) to the stock at the given slot and write the updated three-slot stock with puts.
tasks.note: Start writes the original array. Wrong edit overwrites the slot instead of adding.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that divides rounding up and use it so a partly filled box of 6 items counts as a whole box; the cost stays 4 per box.
tasks.note: New helper before the caller. Wrong helper adds the divisor without subtracting 1.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that tells whether a dice roll (first parameter) is a multiple of 7, and double the points (roll plus base) when it is.
tasks.note: Zero counts as a multiple of 7. Wrong edit swaps the select branches.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that turns minutes since midnight into hhmm form (hours times 100 plus minutes, wrapping past 24 hours), and return the end time (start plus duration) in that form.
tasks.note: Wrong helper forgets to wrap past midnight.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that gives how many units an item is short of the target (zero if it has enough), and return the total shortfall of the four items against the target (second parameter).
tasks.note: Wrong helper subtracts without the guard, so surplus items wrap.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that takes the member flag and the coupon flag and gives the discount: 10 when exactly one is set, 25 when both are, 0 when neither; the bill is the amount minus that discount.
tasks.note: Exactly-one is ne on two bools. Wrong helper uses eq.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that says whether a sample is high (above 512), and return true only when the previous sample (first parameter) was not high and the current one (second) is.
tasks.note: Wrong edit also reports falling edges.

tasks.instruction: On a board with rows of four tiles, moving right from the last tile of a row should wrap to the first tile of the same row, not to the next row.
tasks.note: Keep the row base and wrap the column. Wrong edit returns only the column.

tasks.instruction: Return true when both players are on the same side of the threshold (third parameter): both at least it, or both below it.
tasks.note: Bool eq of two comparisons. Wrong edit makes the threshold exclusive.

tasks.instruction: Rotate the four values left by one place, so the first value moves to the end.
tasks.note: Start rotates right; wrong edit reverses.

tasks.instruction: Instead of only removing the quantity (third parameter) from the given slot, move it: also add it to the next slot (slot plus one, wrapping around the four slots).
tasks.note: Arrays are values; the second set must build on the first. Wrong edit sets into the original and loses the removal.
